segments.display: The same water, again and again
segments.say: Here is something strange. The water in your bottle today may have been in a river a hundred years ago, and in a cloud before that. The earth never makes new water. It just keeps moving the same water around.
When the sun heats a river or the sea, some water turns into vapour and rises into the sky. You cannot see it happening, but you have seen the result. That is why a wet floor dries on its own.
High up, the air is cold. The vapour cools down and turns back into tiny drops. Millions of those drops together are what we call a cloud.
When the drops get heavy enough, they fall. That is rain. It runs into streams, then rivers, then back to the sea, and the whole thing starts again.
Up as vapour, across as cloud, down as rain, back as river. A circle with no beginning and no end. We call it the water cycle.
